title: Separateness of the Benefit Limits Carried by Protection Plans on One Account
content:
The benefit limits of the Pass and Trip Protection plans on one household account stand on their own and are
never pooled.

1. A claim on the plan covering the passes is met out of that plan's limit alone, however much cover sits
   unused on the plan covering the lodging.
2. The season cap of each plan is the most that plan pays over the season across every claim made on it, and
   it is not raised by adding a second plan over a different holding.
3. Where one loss touches holdings covered by two plans, each plan pays its own share of the value of the
   holding it covers, and neither pays for the other's.
4. A household holding a plan that carries family cover does not also count its dependants' losses against
   another plan on the same account.

**The same rule put as a question of assembly.** Ask, of any claim, which holding the loss fell on. The plan
written over that holding answers for it, out of its own season cap; no other plan on the account is drawn on,
whatever cover remains unused there.

**Worked illustrations (hypothetical).** A household holds a plan over a pass and a plan over a residence. A
loss falling on the pass is met from the pass plan's own season cap, and unused cover on the residence plan
does not raise it. Where a single event costs the household both the pass and the residence, the pass plan
pays its own share of the value of the pass and the residence plan pays its own share of the value of the
residence, neither reaching into the other. Where the household's plan over the residence carries family
cover and a dependant's loss falls on that residence, that loss is not also counted against the plan written
over the pass.
